_meta.description: D6 fixtures for google-antigravity / hitl-in-chat. Every leg emits `book_call` — the ONLY tool this cell has, registered by the page through useHumanInTheLoop (src/app/demos/hitl-in-chat/page.tsx); the agent declares none.
_meta.googleAntigravityStaging: google-antigravity staging: the Antigravity Go harness owns the conversation history and never sends role:"tool" messages -- a completed tool call comes back as an assistant message whose text is 'Tool response for <name>: ...'. hasToolResult/toolCallId therefore never fire here, so every leg is staged on turnIndex (aimock's count of assistant messages; +2 per tool round-trip, +1 per text answer). turnIndex is a POSITION disambiguator, not a reject gate (aimock selectByTurnIndex): the candidate with the highest turnIndex <= assistantCount wins, so a leg must carry EVERY absolute position a test can reach it from -- a fresh thread (0/2) AND its slot in a multi-pill single-thread sequence.

fixtures._comment: hitl-in-chat page pill 'Book a call with sales' ("Please book an intro call with the sales team to discuss pricing."). The tool is `book_call`, the only tool the page registers (useHumanInTheLoop, params {topic, attendee}). This leg used to emit `schedule_meeting` behind a `toolName: "schedule_meeting"` gate: the agent (src/agents/hitl.py) declares no tools of its own and the page never registers that name, so the gate could not match — and had it matched, the Antigravity harness would have aborted the run with `unknown_tool`.
